conviction_note: Small net-positive lean. A primary document (the Oct-16-2026 PSU Form 4s) shows FY26 PSUs vested at 100% of target, the maximum, against 27.4% a year earlier ahead of the -6.48% Q4 FY25 print. A Colombian peso ~23-25% stronger YoY in Jul-Aug 2026, which moved mostly after the Jul-8 call, adds translation. Against that: a disputed EPS bar ($1.15/$1.22/$1.27) whose top end is above a run-rate of about $1.15-1.24, a decelerating constant-currency comp (6.9% in Q3, then 6.5% for the June 4 weeks), a soft Central America peer read, and a name that sold its last beat (-0.45% on the Q3 beat). abs_move is set from the 4.49% median reaction, nudged up for a Q4/FY print with Chile capex commentary. p_up sits at 53 because the bar is disputed. The impact sum (+0.3) and the scaled number (+0.3) agree.
bar: Disputed, so every size is capped small. Revenue: Benzinga Q4 '26E $1.51B (page updated ~2026-10-06, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PSMT/earnings-forecasts) vs MarketBeat $1.46B (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-pricesmart-psmt-set-to-post-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/, 2026-10-19). EPS: Benzinga $1.22 (Oct) / $1.15 (Aug snapshot) vs MarketBeat $1.27. The company gives no guidance. Year-ago Q4 FY25 was revenue $1.33B and EPS $1.02, a $0.04 miss (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1041803/000104180325000062/psmt-20250831xexx9911.htm). My own run-rate is roughly $1.50-1.51B revenue and $1.15-1.24 EPS (Q4/Q3 seasonal ratio 0.895 applied to the Q3 FY26 $1.28; operating income growth of 17-20% on the Q4 FY25 $52.8M). That is in line with $1.51B / $1.22, a beat against $1.46B / $1.15, and short of $1.27.
positioning_check: Short interest 1,797,575 shares = 7.02% of float, 7.8 days to cover, record date 2026-09-30 (FINRA published 2026-10-09), down 7.9% from 1,952,036 on 9/15 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/PSMT/short-interest/). That is moderately elevated for a staples retailer but not crowded, and it is covering. No usable option chain: the baseline reports options status no_paired_strikes, so there is no skew. Tape: spot $172.33, run-up -0.37% over 20d and +0.99% over 5d, 12.9% below the 52-week high ($199.84, early Aug 2026, after the Q3 beat). The stock fell from ~$197 on Aug 3 to ~$169 on Aug 20 with no identified cause and has been flat since. P/E is ~32.6 (MarketBeat), a full multiple for this name. Coverage is thin: Jefferies Buy with a $198 PT (2026-08-12), Kansas City Capital downgraded to Hold/Perform in Apr 2026.

findings.finding: FY2026 PSUs vested at 100% of target, which is the maximum since the FY26 plan has no overachievement. EVP Velasco earned 4,666 PSUs on 2026-10-16 against a 4,667-share restricted-stock half of the same FY26 grant (Form 4, 2025-09-04), and CEO David Price earned 11,457. Half of the FY26 metric is total revenue or constant-currency net merchandise sales and half is EPS (DEF 14A), so the compensation committee had seen final FY26 numbers clear both the revenue and the EPS targets ten days before the release. In FY25 the same determination (2025-10-17) vested only 27.4%: NMS of $5,151M missed the $5,200M threshold and adjusted operating income of $237.6M was just over the $236.3M floor. That print missed EPS by $0.04 and fell 6.48%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY25 (2025-10-30), when the FY PSU vested at 27.4% and EPS missed by $0.04: -6.48%. Q3 FY26 EPS beat ($1.28 vs $1.23): -0.45%. Q2 FY26: +2.91%. Q1 FY26: +4.55%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Form 4 footnote reads only 'target criteria determined to have been met'. Seeing that this is a 100% (maximum) vest needs three documents joined: the FY26 RSA count from Sept 2025, the no-overachievement design in the DEF 14A, and the FY25 27.4% comparison. No aggregator carries that join. Had it been priced, the stock would not sit flat and 13% under its high into the print. The limit is that the board's EPS target is unpublished and may sit below consensus, so this rules out a bad year more than it proves a beat.
findings.independence: Same filer family: David Price's Form 4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1041803/000162828026066544/wk-form4_1792531287.xml) shows 11,457 PSUs earned against 1,311 for FY25. The FY25 baseline and the FY26 design come from the DEF 14A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1041803/000104180325000078/psmt-20251219.htm). The 4,667 RSA is in https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1041803/000162828025041969/0001628280-25-041969.txt. One fact assembled from these documents, counted once.

findings.finding: The Colombian peso strengthened sharply through PSMT's fiscal Q4 (Jun-Aug 2026), mostly after the Jul-8 Q3 call. The TRM was 3,132 on 2026-07-31 (-8.96% in July alone, -25% YTD) and 3,050-3,200 through August (3,202.79 on Aug 31), against 4,019 on 2025-08-29. That is roughly +23-25% USD translation on Colombia sales, versus about +14% implied in Q3 (Colombia comps +35.7% reported / +18.9% constant currency). The Costa Rican colon was ~447-450 per USD in Aug 2026 against ~505 a year earlier. Q3's total FX tailwind was +4.0% of net merchandise sales and Q4 FY25's was +0.1%, so Q4 reported growth should get a larger FX lift than Q3 (my estimate +4.5-5 points), on top of a ~8% constant-currency net merchandise growth rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 had a 4.0% FX tailwind, revenue of $1.48B beat $1.45B, and the stock moved -0.45%. Reported-revenue beats driven by FX have not been bought on this name. Part of FX also flows back out through 'other expense' (local currency conversion costs).
findings.why_not_priced: The FX series is public, but with 2-3 covering analysts the revenue consensus is split between $1.46B (MarketBeat), which looks like it misses most of the July-August peso move, and $1.51B (Benzinga), which roughly includes it. If the market had priced it fully, both estimate sources would sit near $1.50B+. The part that is surely priced is the Benzinga bar.
findings.independence: August TRM values: https://www.dolarhoy.co/2026-08-31. Year-ago: https://www.dolarhoy.co/2025-08-29 (4,019.09). Q3 FX tailwind of 4.0%: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001041803/000104180326000030/psmt-20260531xexx991.htm. Colon: https://wise.com/us/currency-converter/crc-to-usd-rate/history (snippet only). This is a macro-to-company proxy that the company has not confirmed for Q4.

findings.finding: Constant-currency comps are decelerating into Q4 against a tougher compare. Comparable net merchandise sales for the 4 weeks after Q3 (June 2026) were +11.2% reported / +6.5% constant currency, against +6.9% cc in Q3 and against a Q4 FY25 base of +7.5% cc (vs ~6.4% cc for the 9-month FY26 run). The underlying cc comp trend is roughly 6-7%, not accelerating.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Comps have been disclosed every quarter. The Q3 print with 6.9% cc comps moved -0.45%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the June number was said on the Jul-8 call. It is filed because the market may be anchoring on the reported +11% rather than the +6.5% cc. If it were fully discounted, the reported-revenue bar would not sit at +13.5% YoY.
findings.independence: Q4 FY25 base of 7.5% cc: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1041803/000104180325000062/psmt-20250831xexx9911.htm. The June figure comes from a third-party summary of the call, not the press release, and its date is stated as either June 26 or June 28.

findings.finding: Peer read: Walmart de Mexico's Central America segment (Walmart's operation in PSMT's core region) grew same-store sales only +2.4% (traffic +2.3%, ticket +0.1%) in Apr-Jun 2026, with Costa Rica, PSMT's largest single market at 10 clubs, called out for a deflationary environment and a cautious consumer. PSMT's own cc comp ran ~6.5-6.9% over the same months, so it is taking share, but deflation in Costa Rica caps ticket growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured link between Walmex Central America prints and PSMT reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Walmex Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) is not out yet, so the latest peer read covers only one month of PSMT's Q4. It is a proxy, and it was public in July.
findings.independence: Walmex 2T26 report: https://files.walmex.mx/upload/files/2026/ES/Trimestral/2T26/Walmex%20Reporte%20de%20Resultados%202T26.pdf. The Costa Rica deflation remark comes from the same report, so these are one document.

findings.finding: The EPS bar is disputed, and its upper end ($1.27, MarketBeat) implies +24.5% YoY on the $1.02 Q4 FY25 base. My run-rate is $1.15-1.24 (seasonal Q4/Q3 ratio of 0.895 on $1.28 gives $1.15; 17-20% operating income growth on $52.8M at the Q3 net/operating-income ratio of 0.60 over ~31.0M shares gives $1.20-1.24). A print near $1.20 reads as a beat on Benzinga's older $1.15, in line with $1.22, and a miss against $1.27. A year ago the company missed by $0.04 in the same quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY25 EPS miss of $0.04: -6.48%. Q3 FY26 EPS beat of $0.05: -0.45%. The response to EPS surprises is asymmetric to the downside.
findings.why_not_priced: With 2-3 estimates and sources disagreeing by $0.12, it is unclear which bar the tape holds. The inference comes from sourced numbers (9M EPS $4.18, Q4 FY25 op income $52.8M, Q3 FY26 op income $65.6M) and is not a document about Q4.

findings.finding: Insiders sold into the post-Q3 rally at ~$190-197. Founder and chairman Robert E. Price filed three Form 144s (Jul 16-20, 2026; the first was 8,399 shares, $1.59M, founder stock, with no 10b5-1 plan date). Director Sherry Bahrambeygui filed 10 Form 144s (Jul 13 - Aug 3; 3,499 shares at $197.38 on Aug 3, a 9.8% cut in her holding). EVP Velasco sold 338 shares on Aug 17. No insider has sold since August.
findings.why_not_priced: These are open-window sales made right after Q3, before most of Q4 was known, so they say little about this print. The amounts are small relative to the Price family's holdings. This is nearly zero information and is filed for completeness.
findings.independence: Form 144 list via EDGAR full-text search: https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=PriceSmart&forms=144&dateRange=custom&startdt=2026-07-01&enddt=2026-10-26. The Bahrambeygui sale: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/sherry-bahrambeygui-sells-3499-shares-of-pricesmart-nasdaqpsmt-stock-2026-08-04/

findings.finding: Expansion cost and capex commentary is likely on the Oct-27 call. Club 10 in Costa Rica (Ciudad Quesada) opened in Aug 2026, inside Q4, carrying pre-opening costs. Montego Bay, Jamaica was scheduled to open in early October 2026 after delays from Hurricane Melissa. Chile already has ~20 staff in leased offices and was posting jobs on 2026-10-16 ahead of an H1-2027 opening at Mallplaza Los Dominicos, with ~$100M committed for three Chile clubs plus a central office. Q4 SG&A carries pre-opening and new-country startup cost, and the FY27 capex outlook likely steps up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 release announced Chile and the stock moved -0.45%, then rallied to its 52-week high within four weeks.
findings.why_not_priced: The Chile plan and $100M are public since July. The size of startup cost hitting Q4 and FY27 is not quantified anywhere. Growth investors may reward the capex, so the sign is uncertain and the size is small.
findings.independence: Montego Bay timing: https://www.jamaicaobserver.com/2026/09/28/pricesmart-montego-bay-open-thursday/. Chile site and headcount: https://forbes.cl/negocios/2026-07-09/la-cadena-estadounidense-pricesmart-anuncia-apertura-de-su-primera-tienda-en-mallplaza-los-dominicos/

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The small positive lean cuts mildly against the flat run-up and the stock sitting 13% below its high with 7% of float short. It agrees with the short base covering (-7.9%) but has to clear a full ~32x P/E and a history of selling beats.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed: EPS $1.15/$1.22/$1.27 and revenue $1.46B/$1.51B, no company guide): every finding stays capped at or below 1 point, p_up 54 -> 53, and print_vs_bar cut from +1.0 to +0.5 against the stricter $1.51B bar.
Rule 6 / rule 3: the run-rate-vs-bar inference was trimmed from -0.4 to -0.3, because it depends on which disputed bar the tape holds.
Rule 5 (proxy and timing): the insider-selling finding was trimmed from -0.2 to -0.1, since the sales came in the post-Q3 open window and are not information about Q4.
Rules 1 and 8 left the PSU finding at +0.8: it is a company-level primary-document number, but the name sold its last beat (-0.45%) and the board's target is not consensus, so it was not enlarged.
